comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific revenue trends for their primary growth segments in 2024, but report opposite directions. Intel’s Client and Data Group revenue decreased by $1.4 billion, driven by lower intersegment ASPs and back-end services. In contrast, AMD’s Data Center revenue increased by 94% to $12.6 billion, driven by higher sales of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While Intel cites lower ASPs as a headwind, AMD highlights volume and sales growth in AI-oriented products as a driver for significant revenue expansion.
